We expect about 13.1 carries vs the 10.5 line. We give the over 61% (needs 56% per pick on Underdog); recent games and the matchup both point higher
rows.why_long: Underdog higher 10.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 61% (draftkings 11.5, moved to this line). Averaging 14.4 over the last 8 games, higher than 10.5 in 79% of them (raw 73%, shrunk 63%). Projects 13.1 (raw 70%, shrunk 61%).
why_points: The pick: Carries higher 10.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (draftkings 11.5, moved to this line) is 61%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 11.5. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 9, 15, 23, 12, 14, 16, 15, 13. Weighted average 14.4; went higher than 10.5 in 7 of 8 games (79% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±4.3, so the line is 0.9 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Projection: we expect 13.1 carries on average; in a typical game 12.4 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 1.9 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 73% and the matchup 70%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 63%, matchup 61%.
Bottom line: we give it 61% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +5.4 points; that works out to about +10¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: The over looks good: we expect about 12.4 in a typical game vs the 10.5 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.
